key_insight: Electrode lattice vibrations can reshape adjacent BiFeO₃ phase stability, providing an independent control knob for ferroelectric nanocapacitors.
engineering_relevance: Engineering electrode octahedral tilts could tune ultrathin ferroelectric switching and transition temperatures; the abstract does not demonstrate solar-cell applications.
method: Use first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular dynamics.
Model symmetric BiFeO₃ nanocapacitors with metallic perovskite-oxide electrodes.
Vary electrode tilt orientation and amplitude while holding elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed.
evidence_signal: Simulations show shifts in the ferroelectric transition temperature and induced antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions, but the abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed to establish whether electrode tilt landscapes can be controlled independently in fabricated devices.
paper_title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
